items.title: Iran war drives Asia EV boost but China slowdown weighs on overall sales
Syria positions itself as an alternative energy and logistics hub to Strait of Hormuz
items.description: Backed by the Gulf countries, Turkey and Washington, Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa is betting on his country's geographic location to turn it into a key energy corridor between the Gulf and Europe, aiming to bring Syria out of isolation after 14 years of civil war.

items.title: U.S. resumes strikes on Iran in retaliation for attack on American troops
items.description: The U.S. said it had struck "dozens" of targets belonging to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps. The multiple flare-ups, after several days of relative calm, raised the risk of a return to all-out war.

items.title: Protest group says 30 dead in Pakistan-administered Kashmir vote unrest
items.description: Deadly clashes reported in Pakistan-administered Kashmir amid first round of voting for regional elections on July 27.

items.title: US launches 'heavy' strikes on Iran after attempted attack on American troops
items.description: After a short period of relative calm when hostilities were paused, both sides have now restarted missile attacks.

items.title: Deadly attack on police checkpoint in Pakistan leaves 15 dead
items.description: The assault on a checkpoint in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa comes days after another deadly clash in the volatile border province, where authorities have blamed a growing wave of attacks on militants operating from neighbouring Afghanistan.

items.title: How well are LGBTQ+ rights protected across Europe?
items.description: After the attack on Berlin’s Pride event on Saturday, the situation of the LGBTQ+ community in Germany is a topic of conversation. How well are queer rights protected in other European countries? An overview.

items.title: Writing on Wall for Putin in D.C.
items.description: Timothy Ash argues that Washington’s growing bipartisan support for tougher Russia sanctions, Ukraine’s battlefield gains and drone warfare edge are shifting the dynamics of the war. He says mounting pressure could push Vladimir Putin toward negotiations as the Kremlin faces rising economic and military challenges.

items.title: At Least 3 Dead in Russia and Crimea After Ukraine Strikes Industrial Sites
items.description: Ukraine claimed its armed forces hit multiple oil refineries, a logistics center and other sites connected to the Russian military.

items.title: How Ukraine’s long-range drones are changing what’s possible in war with Russia
items.description: The latest story of the Ukraine war has been the shift – on the battlefield, and in the adversaries’ minds – wrought by Ukraine’s drone strikes deep into Russia. The goal is to pave a path to a diplomatic resolution.

items.title: Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill Signals Congress United Behind Ukraine, Senator Whitehouse Tells RFE/RL
items.description: As the US Senate prepared to vote on a sweeping bipartisan sanctions package targeting Russia and Iran, Democratic Senator Sheldon Whitehouse, a co-sponsor of the legislation, said the measure reflects renewed bipartisan resolve to squeeze the Kremlin war machine and reinforce support for Ukraine.

items.description: The UN Security Council met on Monday at Ukraine’s request, following recent large-scale Russian attacks on Kyiv and elsewhere.
